author: Bill Sheets
citation: Then, at about 3 o’clock, I was there – Shangri-La! The beach was beautiful, with several big rock formations off shore. I found a great campsite on the edge of the trees just above the beach. The rest of the day was gorgeous and at night the nearly full moon lit up the beach, the water and the rock formations.
location: Edge of the trees just above the beach at Scott Creek / Third Beach area, Olympic National Park, near La Push, Washington, USA
provenance: Newspaper column by Bill Sheets in HeraldNet, published 22 February 2008, recounting his September 2007 solo camping trip to the Washington coast, camping on the edge of the trees just above the beach.

author: Adam Daniel
citation: The live oaks surrounding our campsite stayed darker under the canopy of leaves, but once you walked to the dunes or beach, everything brightened into a muted day illuminated by the moon. From coyotes yelping at the full moon when it finally broke free of the clouds, to the screech owls whinnying through the woods, the night became a nice time to enjoy the sights and sounds.
location: Maritime forest / live oaks campsite transitioning to dunes and ocean at False Cape State Park, Virginia, USA
provenance: Virginia State Parks blog post by Adam Daniel, posted July 07, 2020 (originally 2016), describing a primitive camping trip in the maritime forest near the dunes and beach at False Cape State Park.
